$comment: Rules and baseline for check-secrets.mjs: identifiers no entropy scanner recognises.
aws-account-id: `digests` holds SHA-256 digests, never the id itself. internal-hostname: `domains` arms it;
`published` lists exact hosts under it that may appear. `pending` is a ratchet: `--write-baseline` only shrinks it.

aws-account-id.why: A 12-digit account id in an ARN tells a reader which account to enumerate.
aws-account-id.matches: every 12-digit run, compared by SHA-256 so this file carries no literal

internal-hostname.why: Per-environment hostnames name endpoints that are not part of the published surface.
internal-hostname.matches: any subdomain of a domain in `domains` below, except an exact host in `published`; no rule fires when `domains` is empty

aws-resource-id.why: A VPC, subnet or security-group id is the network topology of a live deployment.
aws-resource-id.matches: vpc- subnet- sg- igw- rtb- acl- eni- ami- vol- snap- followed by 8 or 17 hex digits
aws-resource-id.redacts-to: <prefix>-EXAMPLE — not a hex body, which would still match this rule

deployment-resource-name.why: A resource name from our own deployment maps its topology and tells a reader what to look for.
deployment-resource-name.matches: a name starting with one of `prefixes` below, followed by a letter or digit
deployment-resource-name.redacts-to: nothing — rename it to an `example-` name by hand, so the export fails instead

internal-tracker.why: A tracker URL or issue key cites a record an outside reader cannot open, and names our instance.
internal-tracker.matches: any *.atlassian.net host, and `<KEY>-<number>` for a project key in `keys` below, in any case
internal-tracker.redacts-to: nothing — the citing prose has to be rewritten by a human, so the export fails instead
